settings.name: jmx
settings.description: Compatibility placeholder accepted for configuration files from older Riak Enterprise installations. It does not enable a JMX service in this release.

source.documentation: a dummy value added to riak 2.2.5 to handle upgrades from older riak_ee installs that have `jmx` in their riak.conf

settings.name: kernel.$setup_is_escript
settings.description: Internal flag recording whether the setup utility is running as an escript. Setup computes and stores it so its error handling can choose between printing help and halting the script or raising an Erlang error.

datatype.label: Boolean
constraints: Use the Erlang atoms `true` or `false`.

settings.inferred_default: `false` before setup determines whether it is running as an escript; setup then stores the computed boolean.
settings.notes:
This is the Erlang application environment key `$setup_is_escript` in `kernel`. Its presence in source metadata does not establish a `riak.conf` mapping.

Source review (3.4.1 dependency revisions):

- [setup/src/setup_lib.erl](https://github.com/OpenRiak/setup/blob/76133196bfe9903f8b7914ce3a85d9cffff5dfc1/src/setup_lib.erl#L71)

settings.name: legacyformat_tictacaae_tree
settings.description: Use the older Tictac tree representation for compatibility during rolling upgrades involving per-bucket full-sync. Keep this tied to an actual mixed-version upgrade requirement rather than treating it as a performance switch.

source.documentation: Use legacy-format tictac tree Should only be required when perfoming a rolling upgrade to 3.4.0 or 3.2.3, and using per-bucket full-sync. Temporary option - will be removed in 3.6

settings.name: leveldb.block_cache_threshold
settings.description: Per-vnode block-cache threshold below which memory is not released in favour of the operating-system page cache. It does not prevent memory being reassigned to the LevelDB file cache.

source.documentation: Defines the limit where block cache memory can no longer be released in favor of the page cache.  This has no impact with regard to release in favor of file cache.  The value is per vnode.

settings.name: leveldb.block.restart_interval
settings.description: Number of keys between restart entries in a LevelDB block's key index. This changes the tradeoff between index overhead and key reconstruction during reads; most workloads should retain the default.

source.documentation: Defines the key count threshold for a new key entry in the key index for a block. Most deployments should leave this parameter alone.

settings.name: leveldb.block.size
settings.description: Target size of a data block within a LevelDB SST file. Blocks are indexed and cached separately; this is neither the SST-file size nor the database-size limit.

source.documentation: Defines the size threshold for a block / chunk of data within one .sst table file. Each new block gets an index entry in the .sst table file's master index.

settings.name: leveldb.block.size_steps
settings.description: Number of incremental block-size adjustments LevelDB can make toward its maximum block size. Zero disables dynamic block sizing.

source.documentation: Defines the number of incremental adjustments to attempt between the block.size value and the maximum block.size for an .sst table file.  Value of zero disables the underlying dynamic block_size feature.

settings.name: leveldb.bloomfilter
settings.description: Add Bloom filters to LevelDB SST files to avoid unnecessary reads for absent keys. Filters consume some additional storage and memory while improving negative-lookup efficiency.

source.documentation: Each database .sst table file can include an optional "bloom filter" that is highly effective in shortcutting data queries that are destined to not find the requested key. The Bloom filter typically increases the size of an .sst table file by about 2%.

settings.name: leveldb.cache_object_warming
settings.description: Save cache information, currently open SST filenames, when closing a database and use it on the next open. This can reduce initial request latency by reopening those files before client reads need them.

source.documentation: This parameter enables/disables logic that saves a list of cached objects (currently only open .sst file names) at database close.  The list is used on the next open to pre-populate the cache.  This typically eliminates heavy latencies associated with .sst files opening for early user requests.

settings.name: leveldb.compaction.trigger.tombstone_count
settings.description: Number of delete tombstones in one SST file that can trigger background compaction by itself. Use `off` to disable this extra trigger; ordinary compaction still follows the backend's other rules.

source.documentation: Controls when a background compaction initiates solely due to the number of delete tombstones within an individual .sst table file.  Value of 'off' disables the feature.

settings.name: leveldb.compression
settings.description: Enable compression for newly written or compacted LevelDB data. Changing it does not rewrite existing files immediately; the space and I/O effects appear as files are replaced through normal compaction.

source.documentation: Enables or disables the compression of data on disk. Enabling (default) saves disk space.  Disabling may reduce read latency but increase overall disk activity.  Option can be changed at any time, but will not impact data on disk until next time a file requires compaction.

settings.name: leveldb.compression.algorithm
settings.description: Compression codec used by LevelDB when compression is enabled. Choose among the reported supported values and measure the space-versus-CPU tradeoff for your data.

source.documentation: Selection of compression algorithms.  snappy is original compression supplied for leveldb.  lz4 is new algorithm that compresses to similar volume but averages twice as fast on writes and four times as fast on reads.

settings.name: leveldb.data_root
settings.description: Directory containing LevelDB partition databases. Ensure sufficient disk capacity and write access for the Riak service account; moving the configured path alone does not migrate existing data.

source.documentation: Where LevelDB will store its data.

settings.name: leveldb.expiration
settings.description: Enable backend-level expiry for LevelDB data. Configure the retention period and expiry mode separately; named multi-backend instances can have their own retention settings.

source.documentation: Enable global expiry.  All leveldb databases / vnodes will use same retention_time and/or whole_file_expiry settings. Settings are unique for each leveldb instances in multi_backend.

settings.name: leveldb.expiration.mode
settings.description: Control whether LevelDB can discard an entire SST file when its contents have expired. Whole-file expiry can reclaim space without removing every expired key individually during compaction.

source.documentation: Expire entire .sst table file.  Authorizes leveldb to eliminate entire files that contain expired data (delete files instead of removing expired key/values during compaction).

settings.name: leveldb.expiration.retention_time
settings.description: Retention period, in minutes, before stored LevelDB values expire. `unlimited` disables age-based expiry. This backend policy is separate from tombstone retention after explicit deletes.

source.documentation: Minutes until object expires.  Gives number of minutes a stored key/value will stay within the database before automatic deletion.  Set to unlimited to disable age based expiry.

settings.name: leveldb.fadvise_willneed
settings.description: Use the operating-system WILLNEED file-access hint instead of DONTNEED for LevelDB. It can help when physical memory can hold the database, but changes page-cache pressure for the rest of the node.

source.documentation: Option to override LevelDB's use of fadvise(DONTNEED) with fadvise(WILLNEED) instead.  WILLNEED can reduce disk activity on systems where physical memory exceeds the database size.

settings.name: leveldb.limited_developer_mem
settings.description: Reduce LevelDB memory use for development hosts running many vnodes or VMs. This overrides the minimum and maximum write-buffer settings and is unsuitable for representative performance measurements.

source.documentation: limited_developer_mem is a Riak specific option that is used when a developer is testing a high number of vnodes and/or several VMs on a machine with limited physical memory.  Do NOT use this option if making performance measurements.  This option overwrites values given to write_buffer_size_min and write_buffer_size_max.

settings.name: leveldb.maximum_memory
settings.description: Node memory budget for LevelDB's dynamically sized caches, expressed as a byte size. `leveldb.maximum_memory.percent` provides percentage-based sizing instead; this is not a limit on the whole Erlang VM.

source.documentation: This parameter defines the number of bytes of server memory to assign to LevelDB. LevelDB will dynamically adjust its internal cache sizes to stay within this size. The memory size can alternately be assigned as percentage of total server memory via leveldb.maximum_memory.percent.

settings.name: leveldb.maximum_memory.percent
settings.description: Percentage of host memory assigned to LevelDB's dynamically sized caches. Use `leveldb.maximum_memory` for an absolute budget; leave capacity for the VM, other backends and the operating-system page cache.

source.documentation: This parameter defines the percentage of total server memory to assign to LevelDB. LevelDB will dynamically adjust its internal cache sizes to stay within this size.  The memory size can alternately be assigned as a byte count via leveldb.maximum_memory instead.

settings.name: leveldb.sync_on_write
settings.description: Synchronize LevelDB's write log on each write. This improves persistence against machine failure at the cost of synchronization latency; it does not change replica quorum requirements.

source.documentation: Whether LevelDB will flush after every write. Note: If you are familiar with fsync, this is analagous to calling fsync after every write.

settings.name: leveldb.threads
settings.description: Number of native worker threads used for LevelDB operations. More threads permit more concurrent backend work but do not remove storage or CPU bottlenecks.

source.documentation: The number of worker threads performing LevelDB operations.

settings.name: leveldb.tiered
settings.description: First LevelDB level placed on the slow storage tier; lower levels use the fast tier. `off` disables tiering. Changing the split does not move existing files automatically, so existing data needs a planned migration.

source.documentation: leveldb can be configured to use different mounts for different levels. This tiered option defaults to off, but you can configure it to trigger at levels 1-6. If you do this, anything stored at the chosen level or greater will be stored on leveldb.tiered.mounts.slow, while everything at the levels below will be stored on leveldb.tiered.mounts.fast Levels 3 or 4 are recommended settings. WARNING: There is no dynamic reallocation of leveldb data across mounts.  If you change this setting without manually moving the level files to the correct mounts, leveldb will act in an unexpected state.

settings.name: leveldb.tiered.path.fast
settings.description: Filesystem path for LevelDB levels below the tier boundary. Used with `leveldb.tiered` and the slow-tier path; changing the path alone does not relocate existing SST files.

settings.name: leveldb.tiered.path.slow
settings.description: Filesystem path for LevelDB levels at or above the tier boundary. Used when tiering is enabled; existing level files must remain in the locations the configured layout expects.

settings.name: leveldb.verify_checksums
settings.description: Verify internal checksums when reading LevelDB data. Disabling this removes a corruption-detection check from reads; it is separate from verification during compaction.

source.documentation: Enables or disables the verification of the data fetched from LevelDB against internal checksums.

settings.name: leveldb.verify_compaction
settings.description: Verify LevelDB data during compaction. This provides integrity checking while files are rewritten, with additional work on the compaction path.

source.documentation: Enables or disables the verification of LevelDB data during compaction.

settings.name: leveldb.write_buffer_size_max
settings.description: Upper bound of the randomly selected per-vnode LevelDB write-buffer size. Used with `.write_buffer_size_min` to spread flush activity; larger buffers increase aggregate memory demand across vnodes.

settings.name: leveldb.write_buffer_size_min
settings.description: Lower bound of the randomly selected per-vnode LevelDB write-buffer size. New values enter this memory buffer alongside the recovery log before being flushed into SST files.

source.documentation: Each vnode first stores new key/value data in a memory based write buffer. This write buffer is in parallel to the recovery log mentioned in the "sync" parameter. Riak creates each vnode with a randomly sized write buffer for performance reasons. The random size is somewhere between write_buffer_size_min and write_buffer_size_max.

settings.name: leveled_reload_recalc
settings.description: Use Leveled's `recalc` compaction/reload strategy to discard obsolete key-change history. This saves journal space but adds index recalculation during reload. Reverting to `retain` requires rebuilding data on replacement nodes; simply reverting the setting is insufficient.

source.documentation: Enable the `recalc` compaction strategy This is relevant only to the leveled backend.  If disabled the `retain` strategy will be used, but this will leave uncollected garbage within the journal. The default `retain` strategy retains a history of key changes in the journal, whereas the `recalc` strategy discards that history, but will redo a diff_index_specs calculation when reloading each object. It is recommended to use the `recalc` strategy. This strategy has a side effect of slower startups, and slower recovery from a wiped ledger - but it will not keep an overhead of garbage within the Journal. It should be possible to move from `retain` to `recalc` via configuration change.  However, it is not possible to switch from `recalc` back to `retain` just by reverting the config.  This switch can only be made for new nodes receiving data through riak transfers (not inheriting data on disk) - so a rolling `riak admin cluster replace` would be required to revert to `retain`.

settings.name: leveled.cache_multiple
settings.description: Multiplier of the Bookie cache size at which new PUTs request a slow-offer pause. Used with `leveled.cache_size` to apply write backpressure when the cache is not draining quickly enough.

source.documentation: The maximum size of the bookie's cache before each new PUT results in a slow-offer pause.  Prior to Riak 3.0.10 this defaulted to 4

settings.name: leveled.cache_size
settings.description: Key-count capacity of Leveled's Bookie memory cache. This is a count of keys, not a byte budget; the pause threshold also depends on `leveled.cache_multiple`.

source.documentation: The key size of the Bookie's in-memory cache

settings.name: leveled.compaction_low_hour
settings.description: First local-clock hour when Leveled journal compaction may run. Pair it with `leveled.compaction_top_hour`; 0 through 23 allows work throughout the day.

source.documentation: Compaction Low Hour The hour of the day in which journal compaction can start.  Use Low hour of 0 and High hour of 23 to have no compaction window (i.e. always compact regardless of time of day)

settings.name: leveled.compaction_runs_perday
settings.description: Number of journal-compaction opportunities per vnode per day. Increasing it can reclaim dead space sooner but adds background I/O and CPU work.

source.documentation: The number of journal compactions per vnode per day The higher the value, the more compaction runs, and the sooner space is recovered.  But each run has a cost

settings.name: leveled.compaction_scores_perday
settings.description: How often each journal file is assessed for compaction over a day. More frequent scoring discovers reclaimable space sooner, at the cost of extra background assessment work.

source.documentation: The number of times per day to score an individual file for compaction. The default value will lead to each file, on average, being scored once every 12 hours

settings.name: leveled.compaction_top_hour
settings.description: Last local-clock hour in the Leveled compaction window, inclusive. If the starting hour exceeds this ending hour, the window crosses midnight.

source.documentation: Compaction Top Hour The hour of the day, after which journal compaction should stop. If low hour > top hour then, compaction will work overnight between low hour and top hour (inclusive).  Timings rely on server's view of local time

settings.name: leveled.compression_level
settings.description: Ledger LSM-tree level from which Leveled applies compression. This is a tree-level threshold, not a codec's compression-strength setting.

datatype.label: Integer
constraints: Use an integer from 0 through 7 inclusive to select the first LSM-tree level to compress.

source.documentation: Compresstion Level (Ledger LSM) Specify the level in the LSM tree from which compression should occur. Defaults to L1, so only L0 writes are uncompressed.

settings.name: leveled.compression_method
settings.description: Compression codec used by Leveled. `native` uses Erlang's built-in zlib term compression; `lz4` and `zstd` use their supported codec implementations. Ledger compression can be selected separately.

source.documentation: Compression method Can be lz4, zstd or native (which will use the Erlang native zlib compression) within term_to_binary

settings.name: leveled.compression_point
settings.description: Choose when journal objects are compressed: on receipt or during compaction. Deferring compression to compaction avoids immediate compression work on incoming writes; ledger compression has its own controls.

source.documentation: Compression point The point at which compression is applied to the Journal (the Ledger is always compressed).  Use on_receipt or on_compact.  on_compact is suitable when values are unlikely to yield much benefit from compression (compression is only attempted when compacting)

settings.name: leveled.data_root
settings.description: Directory containing Leveled journal and ledger data for this backend. Include both in storage planning; changing the path does not move existing backend files.

source.documentation: A path under which leveled data files will be stored.

settings.name: leveled.journal_objectcount
settings.description: Approximate object count at which Leveled rolls a journal file. A file rolls on either the count or byte-size limit; the actual limit is randomized at startup to spread roll events across vnodes.

source.documentation: The approximate count of objects when a Journal file should be rolled. This time measured in object count, a file will be rolled if either the object count or the journal size limit is reached.  Default 200K. Note that on startup an actual maximum size will be chosen which varies by a random factor from this point - to avoid coordination of roll events across vnodes.

settings.name: leveled.journal_size
settings.description: Approximate byte-size threshold for rolling a Leveled journal file. Used alongside `leveled.journal_objectcount`; randomized limits reduce simultaneous roll events across partitions.

source.documentation: The approximate size (in bytes) when a Journal file should be rolled. Normally keep this as around the size of o(100K) objects.  Default is 1GB. Note that on startup an actual maximum size will be chosen which varies by a random factor from this point - to avoid coordination of roll events across vnodes.

settings.name: leveled.ledger_compression
settings.description: Optional codec selection specifically for the Leveled ledger. `as_store` follows `leveled.compression_method`; other supported values let the ledger use a different codec or no compression.

source.documentation: Ledger compression If an alternative compression method is preferred specifically for the ledger, it can be specified here.  Default is as_store - use whatever method has been defined in leveled.compression.method.  Alternatives are native, lz4, ztsd and none

settings.name: leveled.ledger_pagecachelevel
settings.description: Ledger level to preload into the operating-system page cache. Choose according to available memory and acceptable startup I/O; loading more ledger data can reduce later disk reads.

source.documentation: The level of the ledger to be pre-loaded into the page cache Depending on how much memory is available for the page cache, and how much disk I/O activity can be tolerated at startup - then the level at which the ledger is forced into the page cache can be controlled by configuration.

settings.name: leveled.log_level
settings.description: Minimum severity emitted by Leveled's logging module. Messages then pass through the Erlang logger and its handlers; backend-specific routing can keep verbose storage logs out of the default log.

source.documentation: Log level Can be debug, info, warning, error or critical Set the minimum log level to be used within leveled.  Leveled will log many lines to allow for stats to be etracted by those using log indexers such as Splunk. Logging will be via erlang logger, and so the destination will be defined by the configured log handlers of the erlang node which starts the bookie. All logs are from the leveled_log module, and so specific handling can be managed using filters on the first element of the MFS metadata, or setting the log level for that specific module.

settings.name: leveled.max_run_length
settings.description: Maximum number of consecutive journal files considered in one Leveled compaction run. Evaluate it together with the single-file and maximum-run compaction percentages, which determine whether a candidate is worthwhile.

source.documentation: Max Journal Files Per Compaction Run In a single compaction run, what is the maximum number of consecutive files which may be compacted.  If increasing this value, the average number of files per run may decrease, unless adjustments are also made to the maxrunlength and singlefile compactionpercentage settings.

settings.name: leveled.maxrunlength_compactionpercentage
settings.description: Retained-data percentage below which a maximum-length journal run qualifies for compaction. A lower value demands more reclaimable space before the run is selected.

source.documentation: Target Percentage for Max Run What is the target score for a maximum run of files, to qualify for compaction.  If less than this percentage would be retained after compaction then it is a candidate (e.g. in default case if 25% of space would be recovered)

settings.name: leveled.penciller_cache_size
settings.description: Key-count capacity of the Leveled Penciller's memory cache. This governs ledger-side buffering and is separate from the Bookie cache configured by `leveled.cache_size`.

source.documentation: The key size of the Penciller's in-memory cache

settings.name: leveled.singlefile_compactionpercentage
settings.description: Retained-data percentage below which a single journal file qualifies for compaction. Lower values require a larger fraction of reclaimable space before rewriting that file.

source.documentation: Target Percentage for Single File What is the target score for a run of a single file, to qualify for compaction.  If less than this percentage would be retained after compaction then it is a candidate (e.g. in default case if 75% of space would be recovered)

settings.name: leveled.snapshot_timeout_long
settings.description: Maximum expected lifetime, in seconds, of long Leveled fold snapshots. A fold exceeding this time may fail when its snapshot is released and old files become eligible for deletion.

source.documentation: Snapshot timeout (long) Maximum expected time for any other fold.  A fold which is taking longer than this may fail as it will be released - potentially allowing for some file processes to delete.  Timeout is in seconds.

settings.name: leveled.snapshot_timeout_short
settings.description: Maximum expected lifetime, in seconds, of a Leveled index-query snapshot. Queries exceeding it risk losing the snapshot; increase only when long queries and retained-file costs are understood.

source.documentation: Snapshot timeout (short) Maximum expected time for an index query.  A query which is taking longer than this may fail as it will be released - potentially allowing for some file processes to delete.  Timeout is in seconds.

settings.name: leveled.stats_logfrequency
settings.description: Interval in seconds between statistics logs from each Leveled monitor. There is one monitor per vnode, so shorter intervals can significantly increase total log volume.

source.documentation: Statistic log frequency (seconds) The wait in seconds between logs from each leveled_monitor (there is one monitor per vnode)

settings.name: leveled.stats_percentage
settings.description: Percentage of requests sampled by Leveled statistics monitoring. Higher sampling improves coverage but adds monitor messages; the monitor has no flow control to protect it from excessive sampling traffic.

datatype.label: Integer
constraints: Use an integer percentage from 0 through 100 inclusive.

source.documentation: Statistic monitoring proportion The proportion of requests to be convered by stats, an integer between 0 and 100.  There is no flow control, so setting this too high could possibly overflow the leveled_monitor mailbox.

settings.name: leveled.sync_strategy
settings.description: Choose how Leveled flushes writes to disk. `none` lets the operating system schedule flushing; `sync` and `riak_sync` synchronize each PUT using their respective mechanisms. Per-write synchronization trades latency and throughput for persistence.

source.documentation: Strategy for flushing data to disk Can be set to riak_sync, sync (if OTP > 16) or none.  Use none, and the OS will flush when most efficient.  Use riak_sync or sync to flush after every PUT (not recommended without some hardware support e.g. flash drives and/or Flash-backed Write Caches)

settings.name: listener.http.$name
settings.description: IP address and port for a named HTTP listener, for example an address in `IP:port` form. Replace `$name` with a unique listener name to configure multiple bindings. Choose the bind address according to which networks should reach this interface.

source.documentation: listener.http.<name> is an IP address and TCP port that the Riak HTTP interface will bind.

settings.name: listener.https.$name
settings.description: IP address and port for a named HTTPS listener, for example an address in `IP:port` form. Replace `$name` with a unique listener name to configure multiple bindings. Configure the matching `ssl.*` certificate and key settings for TLS.

source.documentation: listener.https.<name> is an IP address and TCP port that the Riak HTTPS interface will bind.

settings.name: listener.protobuf.$name
settings.description: IP address and port for a named Protocol Buffers listener, for example an address in `IP:port` form. Replace `$name` with a unique listener name to configure multiple bindings. Choose the bind address according to which networks should reach this interface.

source.documentation: listener.protobuf.<name> is an IP address and TCP port that the Riak Protocol Buffers interface will bind.

settings.name: log_index_fsm
settings.description: Log secondary-index query timings from the index coordinator. Enable it when investigating query latency, accounting for the extra log volume generated by each query.

source.documentation: Enable logging of query timings in the index_fsm

settings.description: Legacy `log.console` option accepted for configuration compatibility but unused in these releases. Configure the current Erlang logger instead; start with `logger.file` and the handler-specific options.
